title: IPO Diagram
body:
Input, Process, Output. One box per task on the [[Structure chart]], filled in before any code
is written.

| | Question |
|---|---|
| **Input** | what does this task need handed to it? |
| **Process** | what does it do with it? |
| **Output** | what does it hand back? |

```
Task: count coins
  Input:   number of nickels, dimes, quarters, loonies
  Process: multiply each by its value, sum
  Output:  total in dollars
```

The point is that filling this in for a task *is* designing its [[Function]] signature. Input
becomes the [[Parameter]] list, output becomes the return type (or a
[[Call by reference|reference parameter]] when there is more than one thing to give back,
since a function returns at most one value), and process becomes the body. See
[[Function design]].

A task whose IPO box is hard to write is a task that is doing two things, and it should be
split. That instinct has a name four semesters later: cohesion, in [[Coupling and Cohesion]].

[[Program design]] · [[Algorithm]]
